about: Planned models from 'Kernel Model Tiers' (pitch doc). A model fills in on the board when any folder publishes results with model name equal to its id (e.g. model='A-S2'). Edit this file to add, rename or drop candidates.

A.name: Tier A · Independent
A.blurb: No current-year NASS data. Past NASS finals anchor the model; this year comes from FSA certifications, crop insurance, drought and weather.

B.name: Tier B · NASS-informed
B.blurb: Everything in Tier A plus current-year NASS inputs that are not the answer: planted acres, yield forecast, crop condition and progress, livestock. Never NASS's harvested-for-grain forecast.

benchmarks.label: Our current model (reversion to the 3-year mean)

models.name: FSA ratio
models.how: Acres farmers certified for grain this year, scaled by last year's ratio of NASS final grain acres to FSA grain acres.

models.name: FSA planted share
models.how: All corn planted per FSA, times last year's ratio of NASS grain acres to FSA planted acres.

models.name: FSA ratio, 3-year
models.how: Like A-G1, with the median ratio of the last three years, so one odd year can't throw it off.

models.name: FSA ratio + stress
models.how: A-G1 corrected for abandonment and switching in bad seasons by a regression fitted on earlier years.

models.name: FSA ratio, same month
models.how: Ratio against last year's FSA file from the same point in the season.

models.name: FSA ratio, national reconciliation
models.how: A-G3's state split scaled to one national FSA x NASS/FSA ratio total.

models.name: Reversion (current report model)
models.how: Last year's acres pulled toward the state's 3-year average: a high year tends to fall back.
features: last year's acres vs the 3-year mean

models.name: FSA pass-through
models.how: Where FSA has historically captured at least 75% of silage acres, carry FSA's year-on-year silage change into the forecast; elsewhere use A-S1. Coverage judged from earlier years only.

models.name: FSA residual
models.how: Corn planted minus our own grain estimate leaves the acres not going to grain; last year's silage share of those acres turns them into silage, blended with A-S1.
features: last year's silage share of non-grain acres

models.name: Reversion + switch signals
models.how: A-S1 adjusted by signals that farmers chopped more (or less) than usual, from a regression fitted on earlier years.

models.name: FSA silage share
models.how: Change in the silage share of FSA-certified corn, applied to last year's NASS silage acres.
features: FSA silage share of corn, this year vs last

models.name: Pass-through + switch
models.how: A-S2 in high-coverage states, A-S4 elsewhere.

models.name: Drought scenario (smoothed level + Drought Monitor chopping)
models.how: Smoothed state level plus gamma x max(0, D2+ share - 0.10) x last year's grain acres.

models.name: Planted × last year's share
models.how: NASS planted acres times last year's share of planted corn harvested for grain. The simple baseline.

models.name: Planted × FSA grain share
models.how: NASS planted acres times this year's FSA grain share, with a correction learned from last year's gap between FSA and NASS.

models.name: Grain-share regression
models.how: Predicts the change in the grain share of planted corn from this season's evidence; one regression pooled over states, fitted on earlier years.

models.name: Monotone boosted trees
models.how: Gradient-boosted trees on the B-G2 inputs, each input forced to push in the direction agronomy expects. Small fixed settings, no tuning.

models.name: Daniel's GBT (reference)
models.how: The team's earlier gradient-boosted grain model, re-scored on the same years for comparison.

models.name: Planted x FSA share, 3-year
models.how: B-G1 with the median correction of the last three years.

models.name: B-G1 + stress
models.how: B-G1 corrected by stress signals.

models.name: Blend
models.how: Geometric mean of B-G5 and A-G3. Selected Tier B grain.

models.name: Reversion
models.how: The current report model, as the reference.
features: last year's acres vs the 3-year mean

models.name: Reversion + acreage
models.how: Adds the change in planted acres and the change in the share of corn not intended for grain (from FSA).

models.name: + season stress
models.how: Adds signs of a bad season that push farmers to chop grain corn for silage.

models.name: + dairy demand
models.how: Adds feed demand: more cows means more silage.
features: FSA silage change in high-coverage states

models.name: Monotone boosted trees
models.how: Gradient-boosted trees on the B-S2 and B-S3 inputs, directions fixed in advance.

models.name: Residual
models.how: Planted acres minus our Tier B grain estimate, times last year's silage share of the remainder, blended with reversion.

models.name: Residual, filled planted
models.how: B-S5 with FSA-scaled planted where NASS has only March figures. Selected Tier B silage.

models.name: Smoothed level + drought chopping
models.how: Smoothed state level plus chopping from NASS's in-season yield shortfall x last year's final grain acres. Never NASS's acreage forecast.

satellite.name: Satellite silage signal (both tiers)
satellite.how: Year-on-year change in each state's share of silage-like acres, from Sentinel-2 harvest evidence on a fixed sample of fields. Added to both tiers as an extra input when it is ready. The field classifier behind it is on the Field models tab.
